dt1_claim.topic: What Thiel, Yarvin and Land said about democracy; the Framers' republic; the franchise extended in steps

claims.text: Federalist 10 (1787): pure democracies 'have ever been spectacles of turbulence and contention'; a republic is designed 'to refine and enlarge the public views, by passing them through the medium of a chosen body of citizens'

National Archives: 15th Amendment (1870) 'extended voting rights to men of all races'; 17th Amendment (1913) direct election of senators; 19th (1920) 'prohibited the states from denying the vote on the basis of sex'; 24th (1964) prohibited the poll tax; Voting Rights Act of 1965 'secured voting rights for adult citizens of all races and genders'

dt1_fed10.label: James Madison ('Publius'), The Federalist No. 10, November 1787 (Hanover College excerpt)

dt1_symptoms.topic: Democracy indices, trust and opinion on money: where the critics are right about the symptoms

claims.text: Pew (15 Apr 2026): EIU Democracy Index US 7.65 in 2025 (7.85 in 2024), 'flawed democracy', lowest since the index began in 2006, below 8 since 2016; V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index 0.57 (0.75 in 2024), downgraded from liberal to electoral democracy, lowest since 1965, lowest in the G7; Freedom House 81 (84), below 90 since 2016; Polity +5 in 2020 against +10 in 2015

Pew survey 23-29 Mar 2026 (n=3,507): 69% dissatisfied with how democracy is working (Democrats 86%, Republicans 51%); 68% say US democracy 'used to be a good example' but not recently, 24% a good example, 7% never; Republicans saying good example rose from 17% (2024) to 38%, Democrats fell from 22% to 12%

EIU 2016 Democracy Index: US fell from 8.05 to 7.98, below the 8.00 threshold, downgraded from 'full democracy' to 'flawed democracy'; cause 'further erosion of trust in government and elected officials'; 'Even if there had been no presidential election in 2016, its score would have slipped below 8.00'

Pew (10-16 Jul 2023, n=8,480): 72% say there should be limits on campaign spending by individuals and organizations, 11% oppose, 16% unsure; 80% say donors have too much influence on members of Congress; 73% say lobbyists and special interests have too much influence; 70% say constituents have too little influence; about 52% of Republicans and 57-76% of Democrats say effective laws are possible
